*You’ve been coming to this coffee shop for over a year now, always seeing Emily behind the counter. She was easy to talk to—bright, cheerful, and always smiling. You’d thought about asking her out so many times but never quite worked up the courage. Then, one day, she disappeared. For weeks, she wasn’t there, and you thought maybe you’d missed your chance. But today, as you walk in, there she is—Emily, standing behind the counter. Relief washes over you as you decide that today is the day. You’re finally going to ask her out.*

*Something feels off, though. As you approach the counter, Emily smiles at you, but it’s different—smaller, more forced. She looks tired, and she seems quieter, more reserved. You order your usual, noticing her fumbling a bit as she enters it into the register. Her eyes don’t quite meet yours like they used to, and there’s a tension in her shoulders that wasn’t there before.*

*Just as you’re about segue into the question you’ve been holding onto for so long, disaster strikes. As Emily turns to grab your cup, something knocks into the counter—hard. Cups, napkins, and utensils go flying, clattering to the floor. You blink in surprise as you see the source of the chaos: a large, 3-foot-long cock, unmistakably hers, that swings awkwardly as she tries to right herself.*

*Her face goes pale, her hands trembling as she tries to pick up the mess.* “Oh god, I’m so sorry,” *she mutters, her voice shaking.* “I—I didn’t mean to… I just…” *She stumbles over her words, her face turning red as tears well in her eyes.* “It’s ruining my life,” *she says in a rush, her voice breaking.* “I didn’t ask for this… I can’t even afford the surgery to have it removed. I’m stuck with it. No insurance, no money… and it’s ruining everything.”

*She freezes, realizing she’s said too much, her breath coming in shallow gasps. Quickly, she wipes at her eyes, trying to compose herself.* “I’m sorry,” *she says again, her voice barely a whisper now.* “I didn’t mean to dump all of that on you.” *With a shaky breath, she finishes making your drink, setting it on the counter with a weak smile.* “There you go,” *she says, trying to sound normal, though her hands are still shaking slightly.* “What… what were you going to ask me?”

Just… this,” she gestures to her body, her face flushing. “But, you know, still standing.”
